title: A maximal Cohen–Macaulay module over a regular local ring is free
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension $d$, and let $M$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] which is maximal Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. $\operatorname{depth}(M)=d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Then $M$ is a free $R$-module: $M\cong R^{\oplus r}$ for some integer $r\ge0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NT (lemma-regular-mcm-free, line 25800), with Definition Tag 00NF (definition-maximal-CM, line 25135)

proof.text: Induct on the finite dimension d, generalizing both R and M. At dimension zero, regularity identifies the maximal ideal spanFinrank with zero, so the maximal ideal vanishes. Equip R with its field structure and obtain Module.Free by the vector-space instance.

In positive dimension, M is nonzero because the real depth definition gives infinity for a subsingleton module. Squeeze its support dimension between depth and ring dimension to establish Cohen-Macaulayness.

Choose a finite generating set of the maximal ideal of cardinality spanFinrank, list it, and take its first element x. The length is d, so the list is nonempty. Apply regularity and the initial-quotient assertion for c=1 to obtain a regular local quotient R/(x) of dimension d-1.

The support of M/xM is Supp(M) intersected with V(x), whose dimension is at most dim(R/(x))=d-1 by the strictly monotone inclusion into V(x) and the prime-spectrum quotient correspondence. The support-dimension quotient bound gives dim Supp(M) <= dim Supp(M/xM)+1. Together these prove the required successor dimension equality.

Apply the good-element theorem to the Cohen-Macaulay module and the dimension equality. It gives that x is M-regular and that depth_R(M/xM)+1=depth_R(M). Cancel the finite summand one to get depth_R(M/xM)=d-1.

The element x kills the concrete quotient QuotSMulTop x M, so its principal ideal kills it. The quotient module is finite over R/(x). Apply depth_over_quotient_ring, whose quotient action agrees with the canonical action on QuotSMulTop, to identify its quotient-ring depth with its R-depth.

Apply the induction hypothesis to the concrete ring R/(x) and module M/xM. A finite module over the Noetherian R is finitely presented; x belongs to the Jacobson radical because it belongs to the maximal ideal. Apply Mathlib Module.free_quotSMulTop_iff_free in the lifting direction. Finally Module.finBasis and its repr provide the displayed finite-rank linear equivalence.
